question: What is the primary smooth muscle that forms the wall of the urinary bladder?
explanation: The detrusor muscle is the main smooth muscle layer of the bladder wall responsible for contraction during urination. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which anatomical structure prevents urine from leaking out of the bladder during the resting filling phase?
explanation: The internal urethral sphincter maintains involuntary tone at the bladder neck to keep urine stored until voluntary release. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which nerve carries parasympathetic signals that stimulate bladder contraction?
explanation: Parasympathetic fibers traveling via the pelvic splanchnic nerves promote detrusor muscle contraction for voiding. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h2)

question: A spinal cord injury at the sacral level directly damages which nerve controlling the external urethral sphincter?
explanation: The pudendal nerve originates from the S2-S4 segments and provides somatic control to the external urethral sphincter. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h2)

question: What happens to bladder pressure as urine gradually accumulates during the normal storage phase?

options.A: Pressure remains relatively low due to bladder compliance
options.B: Pressure drops to zero until the bladder reaches maximum capacity
options.C: Pressure fluctuates wildly with every heartbeat
options.D: Pressure rises sharply immediately after the first few milliliters

explanation: Good bladder compliance allows the organ to store increasing volumes of urine without causing high intravesical pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which autonomic response is primarily responsible for maintaining continence during the storage phase?
explanation: Sympathetic activity relaxes the detrusor and contracts the internal sphincter to facilitate urine storage. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h3)

question: At approximately what urine volume do stretch receptors typically trigger the initial sensation to void in adults?
explanation: Bladder filling between 200 and 400 milliliters stretches the wall enough to activate sensory afferents and trigger the micturition reflex. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the primary action of the parasympathetic system during the micturition reflex?
explanation: Parasympathetic outflow stimulates detrusor muscle contraction to expel urine from the bladder during voiding. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which brainstem area serves as the primary integration center for coordinating micturition?
explanation: The pontine micturition center in the brainstem coordinates the neural signals required for synchronized bladder emptying. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h5)

question: How do higher cortical centers normally prevent involuntary urination during daily activities?

options.A: By sending inhibitory signals to suppress the spinal micturition reflex
options.B: By keeping the internal urethral sphincter paralyzed
options.C: By constantly activating the parasympathetic pelvic nerves
options.D: By draining urine continuously back into the renal pelvis

explanation: The cerebral cortex exerts top-down inhibition over the pontine and spinal reflex pathways to maintain continence until an appropriate time. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h5)

question: What is detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia?

options.A: Complete failure of the kidneys to produce any urine output
options.B: Inability of the ureters to perform peristalsis
options.C: Spontaneous relaxation of the bladder wall during sleep
options.D: Uncoordinated contraction of the detrusor muscle and external sphincter

explanation: Detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia occurs when the bladder contracts while the external sphincter fails to relax, causing dangerous urinary retention pressure. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which clinical symptom is most characteristic of an older male patient with benign prostatic hyperplasia obstructing urine outflow?

options.A: Complete absence of sensory nerve fibers
options.B: Continuous painless leakage of clear fluid
options.C: Instantaneous loss of all bladder tone

explanation: Prostatic enlargement physically obstructs the urethra, causing delayed initiation of urination and a weak stream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T9#GNS121_U2_T9_h6)
